sentence: This project studies how untranslated regions of mRNA control gene expression in different cell types and builds a model to predict genetic variant effects.
This project studies how wildfire smoke pollution affects airway cells and looks for genetic risk factors that link it to asthma exacerbations.
This project builds imaging methods that show how organic reactions work, to help with preparing compounds for drug discovery.
This project identifies neuropeptides in earthworms and pinpoints unique modifications to the genes responsible for neuropeptide signaling.
This project develops a gene replacement therapy for a lysosomal storage disease using a vector that helps package mRNA in extracellular vesicles.
This project tries to find out which cellular defects cause problems in the small coronary arteries of people with diabetes.
This project studies how the retinal pigment epithelium keeps the retina healthy and how essential processes in it change during aging.
This project studies a lectin, a sugar-binding protein, engineered to prevent and treat infection with coronaviruses.
This project studies how social stress affects stress reactions and craving in people with alcohol use disorder.
This project studies when taste progenitors arise during development and how they contribute to taste buds in adults.
This project supports a conference on how genetic recombination and chromosome rearrangements work and are controlled.
This project develops the use of sugar, D-glucose, as a contrast agent for imaging tumors with MRI, starting with brain cancer.
This project studies how a calcium transporter is controlled in tooth enamel development and how enamel-forming cells are disrupted when its gene is mutated.
This project studies how polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolites control ferroptosis, a form of programmed cell death.
This project studies how excitatory and inhibitory circuits in the cerebral cortex drive vision and sensory perception.
This project tests how selective therapeutic agents combined with radiation kill tumor cells in a fatal childhood cancer of the brainstem.
This project studies how epistasis changes the effects of genetic variants in yeast, using CRISPR and chromosome synthesis.
This project develops mouse models of hepatitis B virus infection to study how the virus infects, replicates and causes disease.
This project looks for genetic drivers of when amyloid plaques first appear in the brain, using imaging and genetic tools.
This project develops image reconstruction and deep learning methods for high-resolution receptor occupancy studies of the brain.
